questions.q: What does the brain consistently cast you as in personal narratives?
questions.why: The brain places you as the main character in stories.

questions.q: Why does giving characters flaws attract readers?
questions.why: Flawed characters let readers explore faults, including their own.

questions.q: What animal behavior is compared to human status‑seeking?
questions.why: Chimps watch alphas, similar to human status concerns.

questions.q: According to the book, stories are as common as what daily activities?
questions.why: Stories are as common as eating and sleeping.

questions.q: What effect does believing you are the hero have on self‑perception?
a: It blinds you to personal flaws
questions.why: Seeing yourself as hero makes you bad at seeing your own weaknesses.
